domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m ≥ 2
g is an integer with g ≥ 0
x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) has all coordinates x_k ∈ Z_{>0} (positive integers)
x satisfies the coordinate sum constraint: x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g
in the defining inequalities, i and j range over all ordered pairs with i,j ∈ {1,...,m-1}
for i+j<m: inequality uses x_{i+j} (which lies in {1,...,m-1})
for i+j>m: inequality uses x_{i+j-m} (which lies in {1,...,m-1})
K_{m,g+1} is defined by the same conditions with x_1+...+x_{m-1}=g+1
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer m ≥ 2 and every integer g ≥ 0, there exists a function J_{m,g} mapping each x ∈ K_{m,g} (i.e., each positive integer (m−1)-tuple with sum g and satisfying the given conditional inequalities for all i,j∈{1,...,m−1}) into K_{m,g+1} (same constraints but sum g+1), such that for all x,y ∈ K_{m,g}, x ≠ y implies J_{m,g}(x) ≠ J_{m,g}(y).

shared_context.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously with coordinate sum g+1. Then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.

payload.statement_nl: Let A and B be finite sets. If |A| <= |B|, then there exists an injective function f:A -> B.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let A and B be finite sets, and assume |A| <= |B|. We must show that there exists an injective function f:A -> B.

Because A and B are finite, there exist nonnegative integers n and m such that |A| = n and |B| = m. The hypothesis gives n <= m.

Since A has exactly n elements, we may list its elements as
A = {a_1, ..., a_n}
if n > 0 (and if n = 0, then A = emptyset). Likewise, since B has exactly m elements, we may list distinct elements of B as
B = {b_1, ..., b_m}.

We now define f:A -> B.

Case 1: A = emptyset (equivalently n = 0).
Then there is exactly one function from emptyset to B, namely the empty function. It is injective vacuously, because there are no distinct x,y in emptyset. So the conclusion holds.

Case 2: n >= 1.
Define f on the listed elements of A by
f(a_i) = b_i for each i = 1, ..., n.
This is well-defined because n <= m, so b_1, ..., b_n all exist in B.

Also, f(x) is in B for every x in A, so f is indeed a function A -> B.

We now prove that f is injective. Let x,y in A and suppose f(x) = f(y). Since A = {a_1, ..., a_n} with distinct elements, there exist indices i,j in {1,...,n} such that x = a_i and y = a_j. Then
b_i = f(a_i) = f(x) = f(y) = f(a_j) = b_j.
But the elements b_1, ..., b_m are distinct, so b_i = b_j implies i = j. Hence x = a_i = a_j = y. Therefore f is injective.

Thus in all cases there exists an injective function f:A -> B. This proves the statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Enumerate A and B as A={a_1,...,a_n} and B={b_1,...,b_m} with n=|A|, m=|B|, and n<=m. If A is empty, the empty function is injective. Otherwise define f(a_i)=b_i for i=1,...,n. Since the b_i are distinct, f is injective.

used_external_facts: A finite set can be listed as a set of distinct elements.
The empty function from the empty set to any set exists and is injective.
